{{Quote|Excuse me, please, but you'll have to check that excess baggage. Huh? Oh, I'm terribly sorry. I didn't realize that was your husband. Heh, heh, heh, heh, heh, heh.|G2-4T|<ref name="Star Tours" />}}
The '''G2 repair droid''', nicknamed the "'''goose droid'''," was a model of [[Maintenance droid/Legends|maintenance droid]] manufactured by the [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]] that could be modified to perform a variety of functions. Introduced in the [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] following the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], G2 [[Droid/Legends|droids]] boasted acute intellects that made them wonderful conversationalists but also caused them to be flighty and unreliable. While this made G2 droids unpopular with larger corporations, it nevertheless endeared them to some customers, who allowed their droids to accumulate life experience over [[Time/Legends|time]].

When SoroSuub discontinued the G2 model in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], fan outcry led the corporation to reintroduce the droid to great fanfare [[14 ABY/Legends|two years later]]. A pair of chatty [[goose]] droids, [[G2-4T]] and [[G2-9T/Legends|G2-9T]], worked for the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] travel agency before finding employment in the [[Smugglers' Alliance|organization]] of [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] [[Talon Karrde]], while another team of G2 droids notoriously set up their own community on an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] in the [[Chrellis system/Legends|Chrellis system]]. Other G2 droid owners included the [[holostar]] [[Javul Charn]] as well as the [[EV-series supervisor droid/Legends|supervisor droid]] [[EV-6T6]], who ripped out her G2's [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]] to silence its incessant blathering.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|I had a G2 working for me a while back. It constantly talked about things unrelated to its job, and my circuits nearly fried just hearing it carry on. I had to rip out its vocabulator to finally shut it up.|EV-6T6|<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" />}}
Intended to assist with [[Starship/Legends|shipboard]] repairs,<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> the [[Class two droid/Legends|second-degree]] G2 [[Maintenance droid/Legends|repair droid]] was short in stature, standing 0.8 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] in height,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> a little shorter than standard [[R2-series astromech droid/Legends|R2-series astromech droids]].<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> It was also squat, with a wide, bottom-heavy stance that forced it to waddle when it walked. These traits, combined with its long, multi-jointed neck<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> and widely spaced,<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> weight-distributing [[Limb/Legends|feet]], earned it the nickname "[[goose]] [[Droid/Legends|droid]]." Each G2 unit had a stripped-down, [[Color/Legends|silver]]-and-brass-colored skeletal frame with exposed joints and wiring, with a colored trim. The droid's three-digit heavy manipulators could grasp most repair tools, while splayed feet aided in stabilizing its low center of [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]]<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> and gave the G2 extra stability when dealing with large, heavy equipment.<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" />

[[File:A4-G2.jpg|thumb|left|225px|A4-G2, a G2 repair droid, works on an astromech droid.]]
The G2's most recognizable feature was its binocular head, which contained a [[Vocabulator/Legends|vocabulator]]<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> capable of communicating in both [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]] and [[Binary/Legends|Binary]] [[Language/Legends|languages]];<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> two [[Audio sensor/Legends|auditory sensors]]; and a pair<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> of blue<ref name="Star Tours" /> or white<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptors]]<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> whose improved [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] packages included [[Night vision/Legends|darkvision]],<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> telescopic, microscopic, and multi-spectrum capabilities. Each G2 droid bore a unique identification number stenciled onto the side of its head<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> in [[Aurebesh/Legends|Aurebesh]]<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> or [[High Galactic (language)|High Galactic]], as well as a [[Tool kit/Legends|tool kit]] and a [[Diagnostic scanner/Legends|diagnostics package]].<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" />

Despite being equipped with basic [[Processor/Legends|processors]],<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> G2s units' intellects were so acute that they made wonderful conversationalists. However, this same quality led to a flightiness that made them unreliable in their primary jobs and led them to gravitate toward excessive chattiness,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> though they were still capable repair droids.<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> This feature appeared to be hardwired into their [[Behavioral circuitry matrix/Legends|behavioral circuitry matrices]] and could not be eliminated with [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> Over [[Time/Legends|time]], the droids also developed a unique sense of humor, trading witticisms and bad jokes with anyone who bothered to listen.<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" />

==Role==
{{Quote|Hello! How are you? I'm, uh, G2-9T, fifth-degree labor droid. See, my job is to fix the pilots and navigators for Star Tours. It's a really neat job.|G2-9T|<ref name="Star Tours" />}}
In addition to functioning as maintenance droids, G2 repair droids could be modified to perform different roles. A G2 could be modified into a reliable [[Pilot/Legends|copilot]] by installing a tool appendage tip with a [[Scomp link/Legends|scomp link]], as well as [[Programmer/Legends|reprogramming]] it for piloting rather than mechanics. The G2 could also be used to locate and defuse explosives by upgrading the droid with hardened systems, adding five [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] of internal storage to its chassis, and attaching two tool appendages&mdash;one tipped with a [[Laser cutter/Legends|laser cutter]] and the other an [[Electro-shock prod/Legends|electroshock probe]].<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" />

Finally, G2s could be modified to function as [[Scavenger/Legends|scavengers]] by removing their legs and installing a [[Repulsorlift/Legends|repulsorlift]] unit in their place, as well as attaching a set of [[Electrobinoculars/Legends|electrobinoculars]] and a [[Glowrod/Legends|glow rod]] to improve the droid's visual capability. A removable storage bin or cart on a repulsorlift could be affixed to the droid's back so it could tow the scraps and equipment it found back to its master. As an alternative, a shell could be created and permanently attached to the droid, allowing it to carry up to twenty-five kilograms of material instead of lugging around a separate unit. This option better protected the droid's haul, reducing the chance that it would lose anything it found.<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" />

==History==
{{Quote|We are experiencing unusual behavior from the G2 droids in Sector 2. Maintenance units, begin surveillance of all Sector 2 G2 droids.|Star Tours public address system|<ref name="Star Tours" />}}
===Fan-favorite droids===
[[File:G2-7T.png|thumb|right|200px|G2-7T, a G2 repair droid]]
{{Quote|FEATURING THE NEW G2 SERIES!''<br />"''DILIGENT''<br />"''VIGILANT''<br />"''EFFICIENT''<br />"''RELIABLE|Droid Security Systems advertisement|<ref name="The Adventures Continue">''[[Star Tours: The Adventures Continue]]''</ref>}}
A custom [[Sullustan/Legends|Sullustan]] design,<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> the G2 repair droid was introduced by [[SoroSuub Corporation/Legends|SoroSuub Corporation]]<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> in the [[Standard decade/Legends|decade]] following the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]<ref name="Chronology note" /> and was available licensed from 5,210<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> to 6,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]].<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> Some customers, mostly family-owned businesses or pilots of independent starships, found their droids' chatty behavior endearing and allowed them to accumulate life experience over time,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> with many G2 units finding themselves utilized as pilots and tour guides for civilian charter vessels instead of as repair droids. Many owners even relieved their G2s of jobs and kept them around as companions.<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> About a [[1 BBY/Legends|year before]] the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours" /> [[Sacul Industries Group]] division [[Droid Security Systems]] advertised the G2 repair droid in the [[Star Tours/Legends|Star Tours]] terminal of [[Spaceport THX1138]].<ref name="The Adventures Continue" />

Eventually, a number of G2s achieved an advanced degree of independent thought, resulting in a sudden explosion of wanderlust. In one notorious instance, a team of G2 droids [[Thief/Legends|stole]] a [[Fuel/Legends|fueling]] [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] and set up their own community on an [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] in the [[Chrellis system/Legends|Chrellis system]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> Yet the series' downfall lay with larger corporations considering G2 droids to be a waste of [[Currency/Legends|money]] due to their tendency to talk rather than work.<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" /> These corporations generally had no time for a G2's foolishness and returned the units to the manufacturer, shrinking the line's market base.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> Complaints and a high number of returns from large corporations that bought the droids in bulk forced SoroSuub to retire the series<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]]. However, faced with a surprising outcry from fans of the G2,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> along with near-constant requests from small business owners and other individuals,<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> SoroSuub reintroduced the line to much fanfare just [[14 ABY/Legends|two years later]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" />

===Unreliable workers===
{{Quote|That's the last G2 I'm ever going to buy.|Talon Karrde, in reference to G2-9T|<ref name="Specter of the Past">''[[Specter of the Past]]''</ref>}}
As a member of the [[Galactic Tourist Bureau/Legends|Galactic Tourist Bureau]], the Star Tours travel agency was provided with G2 droids<ref name="Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours" /> by Droid Security Systems,<ref name="The Adventures Continue" /> including a tall, spindly G2 unit designated [[G2-3B]],<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|I|304|G2-3B}}</ref> [[G2-4T]],<ref name="Star Tours" /> and [[G2-5T]].<ref name="The Adventures Continue" /> Despite serving as the [[Foreman/Legends|foreman]] of Star Tours' droid labor pool, G2-4T was given other tasks outside his intended programming, such as handling ticketing, travel visas, and security checks. His sarcastic personality and rude comments to passing customers often got him into trouble with his supervisors.<ref name="Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours" /> Another G2 unit, designated [[G2-9T/Legends|G2-9T]], was purchased second-hand in a "pay-by-the-kilogram" fire sale and was the former property of a [[Troig/Legends|Troig]] [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomat]].<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" />

[[File:G2-9T.jpg|thumb|left|200px|G2-9T was a G2 unit who worked for Star Tours.]]
Although he was much friendlier to waiting passengers than G2-4T, G2-9T's eagerness to engage them in conversation<ref name="Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours" /> and his infuriatingly short attention span<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> often distracted him from his work screening luggage. G2-9T was later returned to the repair work he was programmed for, but his spotty work record continued,<ref name="Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours" /> which angered the company's organic operators.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> When accidents and mismanagement finally drove Star Tours out of business several [[Standard month/Legends|months]] after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], G2-4T and G2-9T drifted between masters before finding employment in the [[Smugglers' Alliance|organization]] of [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggler]] and [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] ally [[Talon Karrde]].<ref name="Convenient Daily Departures: The History of Star Tours" />

A G2 repair droid was used aboard the ''[[Nova's Heart]]'', the private SoroSuub [[Personal Luxury Yacht 3500|PLY-3500]] [[Yacht/Legends|yacht]] of [[holostar]] [[Javul Charn]].<ref name="Shadow Games">''[[Shadow Games]]''</ref> Another once worked for the [[EV-series supervisor droid/Legends|EV-series supervisor droid]] [[EV-6T6]], who was so irritated by the G2's incessant blathering that she resorted to ripping out its vocabulator to finally shut it up. She went on to speculate that a G2's unending stream of conversation was responsible for recent problems at the [[Sluis Van Shipyards]], from where several vessels had departed in the previous few [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]], only to experience difficulty with one or more primary systems just after leaving the [[Sluis system|system]]. Due to increased [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] activity in that area of [[Realspace/Legends|space]], EV-6T6 considered that the G2s might have been working for them, though she had her doubts, believing that they would have already blurted out that information. Other G2 units included [[A4-G2]]<ref name="Scavenger's Guide to Droids" /> and [[G2-7T]].<ref name="Strongholds of Resistance" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The Goose Droids – We were moving pretty fast on Star Tours, and a lot of the things were created as we went along. Wanting droids for our Droid Room, and wanting them quickly, Imagineer Chris Tietz came up with the idea of raiding America Sings one night and grabbing two droids for our show! They got an extreme make-over and became some of the new characters invented for this show. The G2 name came about because of the fact that they were geese from America Sings&hellip;hence the 'G'.|[[Tom Fitzgerald]]|<ref name="Star Tours: Taking Off on a Star Tour">{{InsiderCite|104|Star Tours: Taking Off on a Star Tour|''Star Tours'': Taking Off on a Star Tour}}</ref>}}
[[File:AmericaSingsGeese.png|thumb|right|230px|Disney Imagineering used modified animatronic geese from [[Disneyland]]'s America Sings attraction to create the original G2 "goose droids" for ''Star Tours''.]]
The G2 repair droid was created for the [[1987]] [[The Walt Disney Company|Disney]] [[Wikipedia:Simulator ride|simulator ride]] [[Wikipedia:Amusement park|theme park]] attraction [[Star Tours (real-world)|''Star Tours'']], where it was featured in the ride's queue at each of its locations, which included all of Disney's resorts, excluding [[Hong Kong Disneyland]] and [[Shanghai Disneyland]].<ref name="Star Tours" /> G2-4T and G2-9T, the two original ''Star Tours'' G2 droids, were modified [[Wikipedia:Audio-Animatronics|Audio-Animatronic]] [[Wikipedia:Goose|geese]] taken from Disney's now-defunct [[Wikipedia:America Sings|America Sings]] attraction<ref name="Lightspeed to Endor">{{SW|url=news/imagineering-star-tours-part-2-lightspeed-to-endor|text=Imagineering ''Star Tours'', Part 2: Lightspeed to Endor|nolive=1}}</ref>&mdash;an idea conceived by [[Chris Tietz]] of [[Walt Disney Imagineering]].<ref name="Endor Express">{{EndorExpress|url=star-wars-adventures/star-tours/creating-star-tours/2008/03/interview-tom-fitzgerald|text=Interview: Tom Fitzgerald}}</ref> The droids were stripped of their artificial skin and feathers to help create their droid appearance.<ref name="Lightspeed to Endor" />

The G2 droids originally appeared as controller and worker droids in a [[1986]] ''Star Tours'' [[George Lucas' Star Tours|promotional film]] that aired on [[Wikipedia:The ABC Sunday Night Movie|''The ABC Sunday Night Movie'']].<ref name="The ABC Sunday Night Movie">[[George Lucas' Star Tours|George Lucas' ''Star Tours'']]</ref> As a nod to their design roots, the droids were originally designated "G-2 goosedroids" by the Disney Imagineering project team, a name first revealed in the [[May]] 1987 article "[[Star Wars: The Disneyland Journey, Part One|''Star Wars'': The Disneyland Journey, Part One]]," written by Imagineers [[Bruce Gordon]], [[David Mumford]], and Tietz for issue 118 of the science-fiction magazine [[Starlog (magazine)|''Starlog'']].<ref name="Starlog">{{Starlog|118|Star Wars: The Disneyland Journey, Part One|''Star Wars'': The Disneyland Journey, Part One}}</ref> ''[[The New Essential Guide to Droids]]'', a [[2006]] reference book written by [[Daniel Wallace]], first coined the official designation "G2 repair droid."<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" />

===Inconsistencies===
Despite G2-9T identifying himself as a [[Class five droid/Legends|fifth-degree]] [[Labor droid/Legends|labor droid]] in the ''Star Tours'' queue,<ref name="Star Tours" /> ''The New Essential Guide to Droids'' later classified the G2 repair droid as a second-degree repair droid. Its also established that the G2 repair droid was introduced in the decade following the Clone Wars,<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Droids" /> though the [[W:c:cwa:Droid Programming|Droid Programming]] mini-game in the [[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] later claimed that it was already in use during that conflict.<ref name="Droid Programming">{{TCWA|Droid Programming}}</ref> In both cases, this article assumes ''The New Essential Guide to Droids'' to be the correct source.
